Currency Act
(Chapter 69)
Pursuant to section 17(5) of the Currency Act, it is hereby notified for general information that the denominations and characteristics of the coins to be issued on 2nd July 2005 by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, are as shown in the Schedule.

Milled and bearing the words “MONETARY AUTHORITY OF SINGAPORE” and lion symbol.
The Singapore Arms in the centre with the year-date “2005” below it and the word “SINGAPORE” in the 4 official languages around the circumference of the coin. The position of the mintmark is at 5 o’ clock of the coin.
The coin design consists of a human figure, a stylized globe, NUS Centennial Logo, the words “National University of Singapore” and the face value.
The central feature depicts the aspirations of NUS in striving towards global excellence. The curvatures of the figure are shaped according to the letters “NUS”. The legs represent “N”, the head is “U” while the twisting body forms the “S”. This single figure is chosen to reflect people-orientation within the

NUS community and to depict NUS as One Body. The figure, reaching towards the star symbol in the logo to signify NUS’ quest for global excellence, is unleashed to rise to new challenges. The leaping form depicts a personal drive to engage in life-long learning.
The stylized globe signifies NUS as a global knowledge enterprise that transcends boundaries of space and time. The words on the circumference anchor the central figure, suggesting that NUS serves as a nurturing ground for equipping graduates to thrive in a fastchanging global economy.
